text: An alternative approach to visualizing regression models was devised by modifying the forest plot. Initially developed in the context of research synthesis and meta-analysis, forest plots are typically used to summarize effect sizes of multiple studies (see Fig 2 for an example forest plot of a meta-analysis). The vertical dashed line represents a null effect. Each study is visualized as a square whose area corresponds to its precision (i.e., a function of its sample size). The squares’ positions on the x-axis indicates the studies’ respective effect sizes. Whiskers extending from the rectangles in both directions represent 95% confidence intervals (CIs). In addition, the diamond at the bottom of the graph indicates the weighted mean effect size and its CI [ 17 ]. This representation allows readers to quickly make sense of the results without having to comb through extensive tables.
source_label: Say farewell to bland regression reporting: Three forest plot variations for visualizing linear models
